# Objective

Make the worklog-selection-list plugin's chord shortcuts **extensible per project**: the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` provides the default chords, and a **project-local `shortcuts.json`** (discovered from the resolved worklog root) provides additional entries and overrides. Today `loadShortcutConfig()` reads only the bundled file, so projects cannot add project-specific chords without forking the plugin.

## Problem statement

A consuming project (open_source_llm) needs a `w` chord that dispatches `/skill:wiki-podcast-script --doc <path> --force-single` / `--rewrite <path>` to a pi agent pane for podcast episode work items. That chord is project-specific and must **not** be added to the core plugin's bundled `shortcuts.json` (operator decision). The plugin currently loads shortcuts exclusively from `join(__dirname, 'shortcuts.json')` (see `loadShortcutConfig()` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts`), so there is no supported way to add or override chords per project.

## Users

Herdr users of the worklog-selection-list plugin, and projects that consume it (e.g. open_source_llm's podcast production workflow).

- As a plugin user, I want the plugin's built-in chords (c, n, p, i, r, s, …) to remain available by default, so I can keep the standard workflow unchanged.
- As a project maintainer, I want to add project-specific chords (e.g. `w` → write podcast script) in a local file without editing the plugin source, so upgrades/rebuilds of the plugin do not lose my chords.
- As a project maintainer, I want a local chord with the same key sequence as a bundled one to override the bundled behavior, so I can tailor defaults per project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loadShortcutConfig()` loads the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` as before (backward compatible; no local file → identical behavior to today).
- [ ] When a project-local `shortcuts.json` exists, its entries are merged: new chords are added, and a local entry whose chord sequence (+ view) matches a bundled entry overrides it (local wins). Override semantics are documented and unit-tested.
- [ ] The project-local file is resolved relative to the **worklog root** (the root that `configureWorklogTarget()` / `resolveWorklogRoot()` resolves from `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, i.e. the directory containing `.worklog/`), so the same plugin install serves different chords in different projects.
- [ ] Local file location and merge order are documented in the plugin README (config section), including the override rule and validation behavior.
- [ ] Malformed local entries are logged and skipped without breaking the bundled defaults (same defensive posture as the bundled parser; invalid values never crash or hide shortcuts).
- [ ] Existing chord behavior is unchanged when no local file is present; full `npm test` suite (shortcut-config tests and others) passes.

## Design notes / open questions

- **Local file location:** proposal is `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` (next to `.worklog/`). Alternative: a hidden name (`.herdr/shortcuts.json` or `.pi/shortcuts.json`) to avoid a bare `shortcuts.json` in the project root. The worklog root already has `.worklog/`; a `shortcuts.json` next to it is simple and discoverable. Confirm which location is preferred (see Open Questions).
- **Override key:** chord sequence + view (`'list'|'detail'|'both'`) is the natural key. A local entry with the same chord+view replaces the bundled entry; same chord with a different view coexists. A local `stages` filter narrows availability (already supported by `ShortcutEntry`).
- **Merge mechanics:** `loadShortcutConfig()` currently takes no arguments. Extend it to accept the resolved worklog root (or read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`), parse both files, and merge (bundled first, local appended/overriding). The registry already de-duplicates by exact lookup; explicit override handling must be added so duplicate chords do not produce ambiguous lookups (`lookupChordEntry` uses `entries.find` — the first match wins, so local entries must replace bundled ones at the same key, not just be appended).
- **`code_freeze`:** local entries may carry `code_freeze` like bundled ones (parser already supports it); no extra work expected.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `loadShortcutConfig()` merge logic, override handling, optional local-path argument.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — new tests: no-local-file (identical defaults), local adds new chord, local overrides bundled, malformed local entry skipped, per-project resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the resolved worklog root into `loadShortcutConfig()` (note: `loadShortcutConfig()` is currently called before `configureWorklogTarget()` in `main()`; the call order or plumbing must be adjusted so the local file is found).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the local `shortcuts.json` convention, merge/override rules, and location.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` — no change expected (already passes `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`); confirm.

## Related work

- Consuming work item (open_source_llm worklog): **Add 'w' chord to write podcast script in ContextHub worklist plugin (OSL-0MSHFQ51L009IUOS)** — needs this extensibility to add its `w` chord without touching the plugin's bundled shortcuts.
- **Model selection per shortcut (WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3)** — added the `model` field to shortcut entries; the local-config extension must preserve it (parser already handles it).
- **Code-freeze shortcut visibility (WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA)** — added `code_freeze` to shortcut entries; preserved by the same parser.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the project-local file should live at the worklog root (or a documented sub-path there) so the plugin can find it with the already-resolved root; exact name to be confirmed.
- **Risk:** duplicate chord sequences between bundled and local files must be resolved deterministically (local wins) or `entries.find` will silently pick the bundled one. Explicit override logic + tests mitigate.
- **Risk (scope creep):** full user-level config files (per-user, per-host), hot-reload of shortcuts, and UI for editing shortcuts are out of scope; track separately if requested.
- **Compatibility:** projects with no local file must see byte-for-byte identical behavior (guard against regressions).

## Open Questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (eng/producer):** Local file location — `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.herdr/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.pi/shortcuts.json`? `.pi/settings.json` already exists at the project root of the consuming repo, so `.pi/` has precedent as a project-config location; `.herdr/` is more plugin-scoped. Recommend one and confirm.
- **OPEN QUESTION (eng):** Should the override key be chord+view only, or also stage? (Chord+view is the minimal key; stage is a visibility filter, not an identity.) Recommend chord+view.
data.title: Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Auto-downgrade critical priority when item is marked completed/in_review

## Problem statement

A work item that is marked **completed/in_review** can still carry `critical` priority today. Critical is a signal for urgent *open* work — it drives `wl next` ordering, TUI selection lists, and grouping — so a finished item left at critical competes with genuinely urgent items and makes dashboards misleading. When an item transitions to a terminal state (`status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`), its priority must not remain `critical`.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** who close out work items.
  - *As an operator, when I mark a critical item as completed/in_review, I want its priority automatically downgraded to `high`, so that finished work stops competing with genuinely urgent open items.*
  - *As a developer, I want the automatic downgrade reported in the command output, so that I can verify the change happened.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state — `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` (via `wl update`) or `status=completed` (via `wl close`) — its priority is automatically downgraded to `high`.
2. Priorities other than `critical` (`high`, `medium`, `low`) are never modified by a terminal transition.
3. Command output reports the downgrade: a machine-readable field in `--json` output and a summary line in human-readable output, consistent with the existing `downgradedChildren` reporting in `wl update`.
4. Unit tests cover: `wl update --status completed`, `wl update --stage in_review`, `wl close`, and no-op cases (non-critical priorities unchanged; non-terminal transitions like `plan_complete` leave `critical` intact).
5. Full project test suite passes, and `CLI.md` documentation for `wl update` / `wl close` is updated to describe the auto-downgrade behavior.

## Constraints

- Canonical priorities are `critical | high | medium | low` (see `src/validators/priority.ts`); the downgrade target is `high` per operator specification.
- Only terminal transitions trigger the downgrade — moving `critical` items between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must not touch priority.
- Must not conflict with the existing child cascade: `cascadePriorityDowngrade` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (parent downgrade → children). A completed item is itself terminal, so no child cascade is implied by this rule.
- Prefer reusing existing reporting patterns from `src/commands/update.ts` over inventing new output formats.

## Existing state

- The database allows any priority with any status/stage; there is no rule preventing `critical` on completed/in_review items today.
- Terminal transitions are: `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (`src/commands/update.ts`) and `wl close <id>` (`src/commands/close.ts` sets `status=completed`, `stage=done`).
- A directly related cascade already exists: `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (line ~1230) downgrades critical *children* to `high` when a parent drops from `critical`, reported via `downgradedChildren` in `src/commands/update.ts` (lines ~383–408).
- `wl doctor` validates status/stage combinations (`src/doctor/status-stage-check.ts`) but has no priority-vs-stage rule.

## Desired change

1. Add a small helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal(updatedItem)` or an inline check alongside the existing cascade) that, when an item is transitioning to a terminal state, downgrades `critical` → `high`.
2. Invoke it from the terminal-transition paths in `src/commands/update.ts` (stage/status changes) and `src/commands/close.ts` (close path). Decide between explicit call sites vs. enforcement inside the shared `update()` — prefer explicit call sites to avoid side effects on internal cascade `update()` calls unless a guard makes it safe.
3. Report downgraded items in JSON and human-readable output, mirroring the `downgradedChildren` pattern.
4. Add unit tests and update `CLI.md`.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling (`--status completed` / `--stage in_review`); add downgrade enforcement and reporting.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path sets `status=completed`; enforce downgrade here too.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — home of `cascadePriorityDowngrade`; natural location for the new helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal`) if a DB-layer helper is preferred.
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — canonical priority constants to reuse.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and/or `tests/cli/*`) — unit tests for the new behavior.
- `CLI.md` — document auto-downgrade in `wl update` / `wl close` sections.

## Related work

- `Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced (WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR)` — completed; the direct precedent: same `critical` → `high` downgrade rule and reporting pattern, but for parent→child cascades.
- `Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G)` — completed; priority validation infrastructure (`src/validators/priority.ts`).
- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — completed; critical-priority semantics in `wl next`.
- `Exclude in-review items from wl next (WL-0ML2TS8I409ALBU6)` — completed; in_review semantics.
- `Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added (WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6)` — open; sibling rule about terminal-state invariants on parents.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** `wl doctor` detection/fix of legacy `critical` + completed/in_review items is a natural extension but is NOT part of this work item's ACs. If wanted, record as a separate linked work item (`discovered-from:WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9`).
- **Over-enforcement risk:** blanket enforcement inside the shared DB `update()` could interfere with internal calls (e.g., the child cascade calls `db.update()`); guard conditions must be precise or enforcement kept at explicit call sites.
- **Assumption:** "completed/in_review" means terminal transitions — `status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`, plus `stage=done` via `wl close`.
- **Assumption:** the downgrade target is `high`, as explicitly specified by the operator.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: The request ended with `--priority low` — what does it refer to?
  - A (assumed, rgardler): `--priority low` sets the priority of this new work item itself (matching `wl create --priority low` CLI syntax), not the downgrade target — the feature spec explicitly downgrades to `high`. Source: interactive reply; interpretation documented here. If wrong, the item priority is a one-line `wl update` fix.
- No further clarification was needed; the seed context was sufficient to draft the brief (interview skipped per intake skill step 4).

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)
- src/config.ts — status/stage compatibility (reference only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pure helpers: extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles, isActivePaneMatch, decideDemotion (status, stage) pair.
2. runHydrationOnce(deps) with injectable {runWl, runPaneList, now, log}; fetch in_progress; fetch panes filtered to workspace; outbound-edge stage fetch per blocker candidate (wl dep list carries status only — fetch stage via wl show for each edge not completed/deleted).
3. Apply demotions; wrap whole cycle in try/catch that logs and returns without demoting.

## Dependencies

- Requires F1 (hydrator.test.ts — written first; suite must pass to close)
- Requires F0 (pane-title format amendment — ID must survive truncation)

When the audit runner runs child audits in separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`), each child Phase-1 AC screen spawned a pi subprocess whose output could not be parsed: 'Warning: Unparseable Pi output for AC evaluation — falling back to partial verdict'. The default in-main-slot mode avoids this (child screens are performed by the invoking session), which is how the parent was ultimately verified green. Suggest: make separate-process child screening resilient to the local-proxy output format (or detect the unparseable case and retry/escalate instead of persisting partial), so the mode is usable in this environment.

# Intake Brief — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations

**Headline:** Audits are incorrectly invalidated by mechanical operations (re-sort, sync merges, and other timestamp-churning writes) that bump `updatedAt` without changing the work item's substantive state. This work item fixes all three paths so that audits are only invalidated by actual acceptance-criteria-relevant changes.

## Problem statement

Audits are being invalidated by non-semantic operations (re-sort, same-timestamp merge during sync, and other writes) that bump `updatedAt` without changing the work item's substantive state. The audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats these items as "edited after audit", causing passing audits to read as stale and items to linger in open queues unnecessarily.

**Producer clarification:** Audits should only be invalidated by (a) change in acceptance criteria, or (b) change in code impacting the acceptance criteria.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not appear as "needs re-audit" after mechanical operations like re-sort or sync.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited but invalidated only by timestamp churn.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical operations.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Re-sort does not invalidate audits:** `batchUpdateSortIndices` and the single-item re-sort path no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today. Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run re-sort, assert the audit is still fresh and `updatedAt` is unchanged.

2. **Same-timestamp merge does not invalidate audits:** `mergeSameTimestampItems` in sync no longer bumps `updatedAt` when the merged result equals one side (or converges without bumping). Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` synced repeatedly converge with no unbounded timestamp advancement; existing audit freshness preserved.

3. **General protection against non-semantic `updatedAt` bumps:** Mechanical operations (re-sort, sync merges, audit persistence) do not bump `updatedAt`. Substantive edits (status change, description edit, priority change) still bump `updatedAt` as today, correctly invalidating audits. The `saveAuditResult` pattern of resetting `updatedAt = auditedAt` is preserved. Regression test: audit an item, update its `assignee` or `tags` — audit should remain fresh.

4. **Full project test suite passes** with all new regression tests.

## Constraints

- Surgical changes confined to: `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` (batchUpdateSortIndices), `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` (mergeSameTimestampItems), and `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (if needed).
- No schema changes.
- Semantic edits must still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- Backward compatible: no CLI flag changes required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`** — `batchUpdateSortIndices` runs `UPDATE ... SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed.
- **`packages/shared/src/sync.ts:~L423`** — `mergeSameTimestampItems` sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:1269`** — `saveAuditResult` already resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.

## Desired change

1. In `batchUpdateSortIndices`, skip updating `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`.
2. In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field; converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side.
3. Consider extending the pattern in `saveAuditResult` (reset `updatedAt` to `auditedAt`) to other operations that should not invalidate audits, or implement a broader "semantic vs non-semantic change" detection mechanism. Document the chosen approach.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems` (line ~L423)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), recency scoring (line 2215)
- `tests/sync.test.ts` — Add regression tests for both failure modes
- `tests/database.test.ts` — Add reSort ordering tests for audit freshness

## Related work

- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child)
- **WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS** — Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely (child)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Boost audit-backed items in wl next sorting (established freshness rule)
- **WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V** — Concrete victim example: audited "Ready to close: Yes" now carries stale updatedAt from re-sort (referenced in WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable audit-invalidation policies or per-field granularity. **Mitigation:** Keep this item to the three concrete scenarios; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Checking whether a change is "semantic" vs "non-semantic" could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Simple whitelist of non-semantic operations (sortIndex updates, timestamp-only sync merges) is sufficient for now.
- **Regression risk:** Other parts of the system (TUI, herdr, sync) may depend on `updatedAt` being bumped for certain operations. **Mitigation:** Review all `updatedAt` references before changing; add integration tests for TUI selection, herdr dispatch, and sync convergence.
- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** The producer's definition of "change in acceptance criteria" may need clarification during implementation (e.g., should changing `assignee` or `priority` invalidate audits?). **Assumption:** Only status, description, and priority changes are semantic; metadata changes (tags, assignee, stage, issueType) are not. Document final rule in code comments.
- **Assumption:** The two child items (WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA, WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS) remain the primary victims; their existing acceptance criteria are subsumed by this broader fix.
- **Sync conflict risk:** Preventing `updatedAt` bumps in `mergeSameTimestampItems` may affect conflict resolution if both sides have divergent content. **Mitigation:** Preserve the existing merge semantics for content resolution; only skip the timestamp bump when the merged result equals one side.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which specific audit invalidation scenarios? — Answer (producer): All three — re-sort (WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA), same-timestamp merge (WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS), and any other write. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Bug fix or new feature? — Answer (producer): Bug fix — existing invalidation mechanisms are causing incorrect behaviour. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: When should audits be invalidated? — Answer (producer): Only by (a) change in acceptance criteria, or (b) change in code impacting the acceptance criteria. Source: interactive reply.

# Recovery: classify the proxy "All providers unavailable … time window" 503 as SERVER_ERROR

## Problem

The llama-proxy returns a specific 503 when every provider is outside its scheduled
`available_times` window:

    All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window

The recovery classifier in this repo does not match that wording:

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — `DEFAULT_SERVER_ERROR_PATTERNS`
  contains `/all providers exhausted/i` and `/no provider available/i`.
- The proxy message says "All providers **unavailable**" and "no provider **is** available",
  so neither pattern matches.
- Result: `ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN` → `register-recovery.ts` shows
  `Unrecognized error: …` and performs **no** retry.

This is the follow-up to WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK (which added the generic
`All providers exhausted` pattern).

## Change

Add patterns so the time-window exhaustion 503 is classified as `SERVER_ERROR` (retryable):

- `/all providers unavailable/i`
- `/no provider\s+(is\s+)?available/i`
- `/scheduled time window/i`
- optionally `/outside its available_times/i`

Add classification tests (see `error-classification.test.ts`). Longer term, prefer keying off a
machine-readable `code`/`type` field if the proxy adds one (tracked on the proxy side).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The exact proxy message is classified as `SERVER_ERROR`, not `UNKNOWN`.
- [ ] No regression to existing classifications (all existing tests pass).
- [ ] A test asserts the full proxy string classifies correctly.
- [ ] If/when the proxy exposes a stable `code`, classification prefers it over prose (follow-up).

## References

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts:184`
- Predecessor: WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK
- Proxy side: LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G (stable machine-readable error code)

Discovered during WL-0MU3U1AMP0044WUX (wl update rejected 'in_progress' as an invalid stage).

The wl CLI's valid stages are: idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done (error: 'Invalid stage "in_progress". Valid stages: idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done.').

But packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts STAGES lists 'in_progress' and 'completed' and omits 'done'. Consequences:
1. herdr's stage filter path (fetchItemsByStage via STAGE_STATUS) issues No work items found for the in_progress filter — an invalid stage → CLI error.
2. packages/shared/src/icons.ts STAGE_ICONS / STAGE_FALLBACK / stageColor have no 'done' key, so legacy items with stage=done (2140 in the current DB) fall back to the u+2753 question-mark icon in any path that renders their stage icon.
3. The completed stage is also invalid (it is a status, not a stage); herdr's STAGES/metadata render 'completed' stage icon from legacy data.

Suggested fix: align STAGES with the CLI vocabulary (idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done), map 'done' to the completed-style checkmark in the shared icon maps, and guard fetchItemsByStage for invalid stages (fail-soft, no CLI error). Note the stage → status pairing (STAGE_STATUS) and StageFilter cycling also need review; wl list --stage done with status completed should be verified (done items are status=completed).

# Measure the post-change benefit of mode-aware AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM

## Problem statement

WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME makes the downtime dispatcher pass a mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` to dispatched audit panes: `2` in cheap mode when a second local slot is genuinely free and the dispatch is single-flight, `1` otherwise. The wiring is live in the running `dev` build (herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38; running checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`) — **no `dev`→`main` release is required** for it to take effect on this machine.

The benefit has not been observed yet. The first post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained no dispatched audits, so the audit-only `PARALLELISM=2` path was never exercised.

This item is the operational follow-up: capture a measurement that actually exercises the path.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants to confirm the change raises cheap-window local slot utilisation without increasing remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-change proxy usage report covering at least one 01:00-10:00 cheap window recorded, and a dispatched audit within that window shown to overlap its Phase 2 children with the parent (peak cheap-mode concurrency 2, not 1).
2. Cheap-window local utilisation compared against the immediate pre-change cheap windows and the 2026-08-22_3 reference, and reported (up, flat, or down). Utilisation is measured by **avg concurrency (while busy) = total compute ÷ busy time** and/or **slot utilisation = total compute ÷ (window × slots)**, not by busy % (which saturates at one busy slot).
3. Remote fallback rate compared against the pre-change rate and reported (must not increase).
4. Dispatched-audit Phase 2 wall-clock (per audit, or median across audits) compared against a pre-change sequential (`PARALLELISM=1`) audit and reported.
5. If the benefit is not observed (utilisation flat/down, or fallback up), a follow-up work item is created with the finding and a proposed remedy.

## Measurement method and baselines

- **Metric.** Busy % (union of ≥1-active-slot intervals ÷ duration) is a coverage/guardrail metric only — it cannot distinguish one busy slot from two. Primary metric: **avg concurrency while busy** and **slot utilisation**; plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap. Both are emitted by the proxy usage report's "Local model utilization" section.
- **Primary baseline — per-audit A/B (best).** The change is audit-only, so the clean comparison is a cheap-mode dispatched audit at `PARALLELISM=2` vs one at `PARALLELISM=1` (matched item, or alternating), comparing Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap per audit.
- **Secondary baseline — immediate pre-change cheap windows** (2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24, 01:00-10:00) for the util/fallback guardrails, normalised for audit and request volume.
- **Reference only — 2026-08-22_3** (`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-22_3/`): 04:00-05:00 38.2%, 05:00-06:00 24.8% busy (the source of the cited "25-38%"); cheap avg concurrency 1.55, peak 4. Same-day runs varied widely (`2026-08-22` 49.9%/55.4%; `_2` 38.2%/55.4%), so a single window is a weak baseline.
- **Data source.** Proxy logs/reports live on the proxy host `192.168.0.199` (`/var/log/llama-proxy`, `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable by SSH from the ContextHub machine. Run the report with an isolated `--output-dir` to avoid disturbing the daily cron outputs.

# CLI: treat `--parent null` as detach instead of creating a bogus `WL-NULL` parent

**As a** CLI/TUI user managing work-item hierarchy, **I want** `--parent null` to detach an item (set `parentId` to `null`), **so that** detaching a work item is discoverable and does not silently corrupt the hierarchy with an invalid parent reference.

## Problem

`normalizeCliId()` (`src/cli-utils.ts`) turns any bare token into `<PREFIX>-<TOKEN>`:

```ts
if (trimmed.includes('-')) return trimmed.toUpperCase();
return `${prefix}-${trimmed.toUpperCase()}`;
```

So `wl update <id> --parent null` produces the literal parent id **`WL-NULL`**, which does not exist. The item ends up with a dangling parent link rather than becoming top-level. The only working detach syntax today is the undocumented `--parent ""`.

### Evidence

- Reproduced live during the v1.0.16 release follow-up: `wl update WL-0MTF5WNZV003JKMJ --parent null` set `parentId = "WL-NULL"` (fixed with `--parent ""`).
- Two pre-existing items still carry the artefact: **WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA** and **WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R** (both `done`, `parentId = "WL-NULL"`).
- `wl show WL-NULL` → "Work item not found".

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl update <id> --parent null` (case-insensitive) detaches the item: `parentId` becomes `null`, exit code 0, no `WL-NULL` written.
2. The same sentinel is accepted by `wl create` (`--parent null` == top-level item, the default).
3. Existing detach syntax `--parent ""` continues to work unchanged (backwards compatible).
4. A genuinely invalid parent id (e.g. a non-existent `WL-XXXX`) still fails as today — no behaviour change there.
5. `--parent` help text documents the detach form; `CLI.md` and `EXAMPLES.md` document it.
6. `wl doctor` detects dangling `WL-NULL` (or any non-existent) parent references and proposes a fix; the two known items are remediated.

## Suggested implementation

- Add a small `normalizeParentId(value, prefix)` helper (in `src/cli-utils.ts`) that maps case-insensitive `null` / `none` / `nil` / `-` (and empty string) to `null`, otherwise delegates to `normalizeCliId()`.
- Use it at both call sites: `src/commands/update.ts` (`parentCandidate`, ~L163) and `src/commands/create.ts` (`parentId`, ~L198).
- Keep `normalizeCliId()` unchanged so other id fields are unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wl update <id> --parent null --json` sets `parentId: null`; `wl show <id> --json` confirms; no item is created or referenced as `WL-NULL`.
2. `wl create --title "x" --parent null --json` creates a top-level item (`parentId: null`).
3. `wl update <id> --parent ""` and `--parent none` both detach (documented aliases).
4. `wl update <id> --parent WL-DOESNOTEXIST` still errors (unchanged).
5. Unit tests for the new helper cover `null`, `NULL`, `none`, `-`, `""`, and a real/partial id.
6. CLI integration tests cover update-detach and create-top-level via `--parent null`.
7. `--parent` help text and `CLI.md`/`EXAMPLES.md` document detach.
8. `wl doctor` flags existing `WL-NULL` parent references; WL-0MLGTKNKF14R37IA and WL-0MLGTKO880HYPZ2R are cleaned to `parentId: null`.
9. `npm run build` and the full suite pass (build → test → commit order).

## Key files

- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `normalizeCliId`; add `normalizeParentId`
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L163)
- `src/commands/create.ts` — `--parent` handling (~L198)
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — dangling-parent check
- `tests/unit/cli-args.test.ts` (or equivalent) — helper unit tests
- `tests/cli/` — update/create integration tests
- `CLI.md`, `EXAMPLES.md`

## Notes

- Discovered during the ContextHub v1.0.16 release follow-up (WL-0MUJKVZTZ003FX8S); the same `--parent null` mistake was made while detaching the four hydrator follow-ups.
- `--parent null` for `wl list` / `wl search` (filter for root items) is a separate semantics question and is out of scope here.

# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect (AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ)

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.

   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
3. "Outstanding audit" is determined by the existing audit-freshness semantics
   (`isAuditFresh` / `inReviewBucket`): an `in_review` item with no stored
   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A
   fresh, passed audit does not.

## Headline

The recovery-extension crash fixed for `_notifyFn` (WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B) may be
one of several retained-`ctx` async paths. Audit the recovery module (and
adjacent Worklog extension code) for other captured/stored `ExtensionContext`
references that are invoked asynchronously after a session replacement/reload,
and harden them with the same defensively-guarded pattern.

## Context / Discovered from

- **Discovered from:** WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B (stale-ctx `_notifyFn` crash). The
  parent deliberately scoped only the `_notifyFn` notify path and recorded
  broader stale-ctx hardening as separate work (see the parent's
  "Risks & Assumptions" section: "record broader stale-ctx hardening as

## Goal (user story)

**As a pi extension maintainer**, I want every asynchronous path in the Worklog
recovery extension that can outlive its original `ExtensionContext` to degrade
gracefully (skip the operation) rather than throw an uncaught exception, so
that a session replacement/reload cannot crash a headless pi run.

- A written audit enumerates every module-level or long-lived reference to a
  handler `ctx` (or a closure capturing it) in
  `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/` and classifies each as either **safe**

  from a timer/async callback after the handler returns).

  WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B or recorded as a new blocking work item with rationale.

  stale/invalidated ctx, operation skipped).
- No change to retry semantics, backoff, attempt counts, or
  abort/session-generation guards.
- The Worklog extension test suite passes and the full project test suite
  passes with the changes.

## Out of scope

# Honour long server `Retry-After` hints (do not clamp to 60 s) so the client waits until models return

Linked from llm-proxy intake `LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI` (producer decision Q3a).

## Problem

The Worklog recovery retry loop clamps *every* retry delay to the category's
`maxDelayMs`. For the retryable `serverError` / `timeout` categories that cap is
**60 000 ms** (`DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG` in
`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`), and the
server-hint path applies it too:

```ts
// retry-logic.ts -> calculateDelay()
const jittered = serverHintMs * (1 + jitterRatio * random());
return Math.min(Math.round(jittered), config.maxDelayMs);
```

The llm-proxy now emits a **truthful** `Retry-After` / `retry_after` on the
"All providers exhausted" 503, derived from real availability
(`_compute_retry_after`: cooldown durations, `available_times` window edges,
usage-limit reset times). During the overnight UTC gaps that value is **minutes
to hours**, not seconds.

Because the retry loop is unbounded (`while (true)` in
`register-recovery.ts`) but the applied delay is clamped to 60 s, a client that
is correctly told "come back in 3 hours" instead retries ~every 60 s for the
whole gap, re-emits `SERVER_ERROR` notifications and never actually sleeps until
models return. The proxy's honest retry timer is therefore not honoured for
multi-minute/multi-hour waits.

## Change

When a usable server hint is present, **honour the full hint** rather than
clamping it to the local exponential cap:

- Keep the local exponential cap (`baseDelayMs`/`maxDelayMs`) for the
  **no-hint** path, unchanged.
- For server-hint-derived delays, allow the delay to exceed `maxDelayMs` up to a
  deliberately large (or configurable/unbounded) ceiling, so a multi-hour
  `Retry-After` is actually waited out (the sleep remains interruptible, so
  ESC/session change still aborts promptly).
- Optionally add a separate configurable ceiling for server hints (e.g.
  `serverHintMaxDelayMs`, default "no additional cap" or a long bound such as
  the overnight-gap maximum), with the upward jitter retained to avoid lockstep
  retries.
- Keep the hint authoritative: it must not be combined with the local
  exponential (existing behaviour).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A server `Retry-After`/`retry_after` hint longer than `maxDelayMs` is
      honoured in full (the applied delay equals the hinted delay plus the
      configured upward jitter, not the 60 s cap).
- [ ] The no-hint path still uses the exponential backoff capped at
      `maxDelayMs` (no behaviour change).
- [ ] The sleep remains interruptible by user abort (ESC) and session switch,
      including for multi-minute waits.
- [ ] Tests cover: hint > cap honoured; hint < cap unchanged; hint absent ->
      exponential; jitter applied upward only; interrupt during a long wait.
- [ ] Any new config option is documented in the recovery module docs/comments.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — `calculateDelay`,
  `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG`, `resolveRetryDelay`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — the retry
  loop that consumes `resolveRetryDelay`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/*.test.ts` — extend tests.

## References

- llm-proxy item: `LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI` (retry timer on "no available models"),
  parent epic `LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO`.
- Proxy retry-timer predecessors: `LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4` (honest Retry-After),
  `LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G` (stable code), `LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08` (chain-hold bound).
- Related client work: `WL-0MU9Z7L8X00117BI` (honour Retry-After on startup ramp),
  `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK` / `WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W` (classify exhaustion 503).

# wl doctor reports no issues when pending wl doctor upgrade migrations/hooks exist

## Problem statement

The top-level `wl doctor` validation command checks only work-item status/stage
compatibility, dependency edges, and priority. It does not check whether
`wl doctor upgrade` has pending database schema migrations or outdated git hooks.
When work items are otherwise clean it prints `Doctor: no issues found.`, giving
operators and automated health checks a false all-clear while upgrades remain
outstanding.

## Users

- **Operators / agents** running `wl doctor` as the routine health check.
  - User story: "As an operator, when I run `wl doctor` I want to be told that
    schema migrations or git hooks are pending so I can apply them with
    `wl doctor upgrade` before the database or hooks drift further."
- **CI / automation** invoking `wl doctor --json` to gate or report project health.

    so I can surface a remediation step."

1. The top-level `wl doctor` action detects pending schema migrations (via
   `listPendingMigrations()`) and outdated git hooks (via `detectHooksTargetDir()`
   + `dryRunHooks()`), and, when either is present, prints an actionable notice
   instructing the user to run `wl doctor upgrade`.
2. When there are no validation findings but pending upgrades exist, `wl doctor`
   must NOT conclude with only `Doctor: no issues found.`; it must also report the
   pending upgrades and the `wl doctor upgrade` instruction.
3. The pending-upgrade notice is surfaced whenever pending upgrades exist —
   including when validation findings are also present — without changing the
   existing per-item validation findings output.
4. `wl doctor --json` continues to emit a single, parseable JSON document with no
   preamble or trailing text, and includes machine-readable pending-upgrade
   information (pending migration count/ids and outdated hook count) in an
   additive, backward-compatible way.
5. `wl doctor` exits with status 0 when only pending upgrades are found (the notice
   is advisory, mirroring `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run`); no existing exit-code
   behaviour changes.
6. Automated tests cover: (a) doctor reports pending migrations and instructs
   `wl doctor upgrade`; (b) doctor reports outdated hooks; (c) doctor reports
   nothing extra when fully up to date; (d) `wl doctor --json` remains valid JSON
   and carries the pending-upgrade data.

   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

  reports and instructs. Applying remains the job of `wl doctor upgrade`.
- Must not regress the pure-JSON contract: no stdout preamble/trailing text in
  `--json` mode.
- Must run within `utils.requireInitialized()` and must degrade gracefully when
  not in a git repo or when the DB file is absent (no crash).
- Follow the ephemeral-JSONL/SQLite architecture (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`).

## Existing state

- `src/commands/doctor.ts` defines the parent `doctor` action and subcommands
  `upgrade`, `stage-sync`, `prune`, `foreign-items`, `audit-gaps`, `priority`,
  `file-paths`, `migrate`.

  `validateDependencyEdges`, and priority validation, then prints
  `Doctor: no issues found.` when empty, or grouped findings otherwise. It does
  **not** call `listPendingMigrations` or `dryRunHooks`.
- `wl doctor upgrade` already uses `listPendingMigrations()`,
  `detectHooksTargetDir()` and `dryRunHooks('.githooks', hooksTargetDir)` and
  reports `hasPendingMigrations` / `hasOutdatedHooks`.

  purity only.

  state:
  - `const pending = listPendingMigrations();`
  - `const hooks = dryRunHooks('.githooks', detectHooksTargetDir());`

  and the `wl doctor upgrade` instruction). When there are no validation findings,
  print the pending notice instead of a bare `Doctor: no issues found.`; when
  findings exist, append the notice after the findings/manual-fix sections.

  additively. Preferred approach: retain the findings array and append a synthetic
  finding with a stable `checkId` (e.g. `upgrade.pending`), a human `message`, and

# Own-backlog dispatch fallback must relinquish leadership

discovered-from:WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9

## Problem statement

WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 restricted downtime dispatch to the operator's sprint-view
window: when nothing in the view is dispatchable the dispatcher no-ops. The
operator has explicitly accepted that starvation trade-off **for that item**
(a non-critical item outside the visible sprint may go undispatched).

This item adds a bounded escape valve with a fairness guard:

> If there are no work items available to the dispatcher (nothing dispatchable
> in the sprint view), it may choose work from **its own backlog**. Once it has
> dispatched something from its own backlog, it must **relinquish the leadership
> role** so another instance can take over leadership.

The intent is to let the fleet keep working when a single root's sprint view is
momentarily empty/blocked, without any one instance monopolising leadership by
continually reaching into its own hidden backlog.

## User stories

- *As an operator*, when my sprint view is empty or fully blocked, I want the
  leader to still be able to pick up work from its own backlog, so capacity is
  not wasted.
- *As an operator*, once the leader has used that privilege, I want it to hand
  leadership over, so dispatch is shared fairly across instances.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Own-backlog fallback when the view is empty.** When the sprint-view head
   yields no dispatchable candidate (the existing terminal reasons —
   `no-candidate`, `review-queue-hold`, `code-freeze`, `fresh-audit-skip`,
   `audit-in-flight`, `audit-host-saturated`, `in-flight-hold` — or a genuinely
   empty view), the leader MAY fall back to its **own worklog backlog** (items
   beyond the sprint-view window). Verification: unit tests assert that with an
   empty/fully-filtered in-view head and an eligible out-of-view item in the
   leader's own root, the item is dispatched.

2. **Fallback is scoped to the leader's OWN root.** The fallback never reads or
   dispatches another instance's or another worklog root's hidden backlog.
   Verification: tests assert the fallback head lookup is made against the
   leader's own `cwd`/root only.

3. **Canonical ranking preserved.** The fallback re-reads the SAME ranking path
   (`fetchNextItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems`) with a bounded
   larger window; it is a window extension, never a second ranking. Verification:
   ordering assertions on the fallback candidate.

4. **Leadership is relinquished after an own-backlog dispatch.** On a successful
   dispatch sourced from the own backlog (not from a normal in-view candidate),
   the instance MUST voluntarily step down via the existing
   `LeaderElectionManager.releaseLeadership()` so another instance can win the
   next election. Verification: a test asserts `releaseLeadership()` is called
   exactly once after a successful own-backlog dispatch, and NOT called after a
   normal in-view dispatch.

5. **Step-down never undoes the dispatch.** The claim / dispatch marker / spawn
   for the own-backlog item are completed before (or atomically with) the
   hand-off; the step-down must not roll back a pending dispatch, and the
   dispatched pane is not orphaned. Verification: after the fallback dispatch the
   item is claimed/marked and a pane is spawned, while the next tick observes the
   instance as non-leader.

6. **No step-down when the fallback finds nothing.** If no eligible own-backlog
   item exists, leadership is retained and the existing terminal reason is
   reported unchanged. Verification: tests assert no `releaseLeadership()` call
   and the pre-existing reason.

7. **All existing safety gates still apply** to the own-backlog candidate as
   sequential filters: scheduled-prompt, code-freeze, producer-review,
   dispatched-marker, per-tier free-slot minimums, active-audit single-flight,
   audit-host saturation, freshness/recency, CAS claim, spawn. Verification: the
   existing gate tests continue to pass unmodified, plus one integration test
   that a gated out-of-view item is still filtered.

8. **Critical behaviour unchanged.** `critical` items remain mandatory in the
   view with the existing critical-first escalation; this fallback is only for
   the no-dispatchable-in-view case. Verification: existing critical-first tests
   pass unmodified.

9. **Bounded and fail-open.** The fallback window is bounded (reuse/extend
   `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` or a new named bound); a `{ok:false}` lookup, a
   thrown error, or an empty fallback head degrades to the original terminal
   reason and never panics. Verification: fail-open tests.

10. **Documentation updated** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the
    own-backlog fallback + leadership hand-off contract, and
    `packages/herdr/README.md` matches.

11. **Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- **No second ranking.** Reuse the canonical Herdr ranking path with a larger
  window; safety gates remain filters, never a fallback ordering.
- **Reuse the existing election primitive.** Use
  `LeaderElectionManager.releaseLeadership()` (`leader-election.ts`); do not
  invent a new hand-off mechanism or persistence.
- **Own root only.** `browseItemCount` remains the view bound; the fallback
  deliberately reads beyond it, but only from the instance's own worklog root.
- **Fail-open preserved.** A fallback lookup failure must not convert a defined
  outcome into a new failure.
- **No new persistence mechanism** and no coordination-file schema change.
- **No regressions** to TUI rendering or the existing sprint-view-only contract.

## Assumptions (to confirm at intake)

- **A1:** The fallback targets the highest-ranked eligible item from the leader's
  own backlog (canonical ranking), not an arbitrary pick — "anything from its own
  backlog" means "not restricted to the sprint-view window", not "random".
- **A2:** "Relinquish leadership" is a voluntary step-down
  (`releaseLeadership()`), clearing the lease/lock so the next election is won by
  another instance; the instance may re-acquire on a later tick under the normal
  election rules.
- **A3:** The step-down happens once per successful own-backlog dispatch, in the
  same tick as the spawn, and does not trigger an immediate self re-election in
  that tick.

## Open questions

- **Q1:** Does the fallback apply in legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`, the
  instance is always "leader" with no peers)? Options: (A) coordination/leader
  mode only — legacy keeps today's NOP; (B) both, but legacy skips the step-down
  (no peer to hand to). *Assumed: A.*
- **Q2:** If there is no other eligible instance to take over, should the leader
  still step down (risking an idle fleet), or retain leadership? Assumed: step
  down only when at least one peer instance is present/eligible; otherwise
  retain.
- **Q3:** Should own-backlog fallback dispatch be rate-limited (e.g. at most one
  per N minutes) to bound leadership churn? Assumed: no extra rate limit beyond
  the existing no-candidate cooldown; revisit if churn is observed.

## Risks

- **Leadership churn.** Frequent fallback dispatches could cause repeated
  elections and idle windows. *Mitigation:* fallback only fires when the view is
  empty, at most one step-down per fallback dispatch, subject to the existing
  election backoff; Q3 rate-limiting if needed.
- **Fairness vs. throughput.** Stepping down when no peer can take over would
  idle the machine. *Mitigation:* Q2 (retain when no eligible peer).
- **Root leakage.** A naive implementation could dispatch another root's hidden
  backlog. *Mitigation:* AC2 own-root-only tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — fallback read + dispatch in
  `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchFromCoordination` / the leader loop; wire the
  step-down after an own-backlog dispatch; possibly extend
  `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` usage.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — existing `releaseLeadership()`
  (reused, likely no change).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getHerdrListHead` / deps wiring if a
  separate fallback limit is needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.test.ts` — fallback + step-down tests.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — contract docs.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9** (completed/in_review) — sprint-view-only dispatch
  window; accepted the starvation trade-off this item relieves. Discovered-from
  source.
- **WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5** (completed) — original extended dispatch window
  (removed/restricted for non-critical work by WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9). This item
  reintroduces a *bounded, own-root, leadership-handing-off* fallback rather than
  the previous unconditional extension.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** (completed) — "dispatcher == Herdr list head; gates
  are filters" contract.
- **WL-0MTMPSCL8000O45H** — coordination check-in / leader lease cadence.

# a-r (audit reject) should not change work item priority

## Problem statement

The herdr `a-r` ("audit reject") chord silently overwrites the selected work
item's priority with `medium`. Rejecting an item for rework should reset its
lifecycle state (`open` / `plan_complete`) but must preserve the priority the
producer already assigned, so that a `high` or `critical` item is not
downgraded by the act of rejecting it.

## Users

Producers reviewing `in_review` work items in herdr.

- As a producer, when I press `a-r` to reject an item for rework, I want its
  priority to remain unchanged, so that the triage/urgency signal I set is not
  lost.
- As a producer, when I reject a `critical` item, I want it to stay `critical`
  so it re-enters the queue with the correct urgency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `a-r` (audit reject) shortcut command no longer passes `--priority` to
   `wl update`; a rejected item's priority is left unchanged.
2. The `a-r` shortcut still resets the item's `status` to `open` and `stage`
   to `plan_complete`, and still runs `wl reviewed <id> false` and
   `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` with the rejection summary.
3. The `a-r` shortcut label/description no longer claim a priority reset
   (description reads "reset it to open/plan_complete for rework").
4. Shortcut-config, worklist and herdr shortcut tests are updated to assert the
   priority-preserving behaviour; no test asserts the removed `--priority medium`
   token.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Change is confined to the bundled shortcut definition and its test fixtures.
- Backwards compatibility for `wl update --priority <level>` is unaffected; only
  the `a-r` shortcut stops supplying the flag.
- Keep the `a-y` (audit approve) behaviour unchanged — it already does not
  touch priority.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` defines the `a-r` chord as:

```text
!!wl reviewed <id> false && wl update <id> --status open --stage plan_complete --priority medium && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no --summary 'Rejected by manual review. <reason>'
```

with description "Reject the in_review item and reset it to
open/plan_complete/medium for rework." This was deliberately introduced by the
now-completed work item WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 ("a-r (audit reject) should reset
item to open/plan_complete/medium"); the priority reset is now considered
undesirable because it destroys the producer's priority signal.

## Desired change

Drop the `--priority medium` token from the `a-r` command chain and update the
shortcut description accordingly, so rejection preserves the item's priority.
Update the affected test fixtures and assertions to match.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Remove `--priority medium` from the `a-r` command; update its `description`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Update the two `a-r` assertions (WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2 tests) to expect no `--priority` token.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Update the `a-r` compound-command fixture/resolved command.
- `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts` — Update the `a-r` fixture and resolved-command expectation.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Confirm no documented claim of a priority reset; adjust if present.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSM72QXN008GUP2** — "a-r (audit reject) should reset item to open/plan_complete/medium" (completed). Introduced the `--priority medium` token this item removes; direct predecessor.
- **WL-0MU7KEX65004X0U9** — rejection reasons with apostrophes no longer break the audit reject shortcut (completed). Same chord.
- **WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV** — audit fingerprint repair affecting the `a-y`/`a-r` background shortcuts (completed). Same chord.
- **WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8** — shortcut commands not refreshing the selection list; listed `a-r` among modifying chords (completed).
- **WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL** — `open_pane: false` background dispatch, used by `a-r`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLX5OADB1TECIZV** – Testing: automation - create work item (completed)
- **WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G** – Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (completed)

## Risks & assumptions

# Add a CTA field to the project config

## Problem statement

Worklog has no first-class way to declare a per-project call-to-action (CTA) for
release/report output. Game projects need a consistent, project-specific prompt
("play the alpha, give feedback") to appear in reports such as release
notifications, but today every repository would have to hard-code that text.
Adding a typed, documented `cta` config field gives projects one place to define
it and gives report consumers a single resolver to read it from.

## Users

- **Game producer / release manager** — sets a per-project CTA so release output
  consistently invites players to try the alpha and give feedback.
  - *As a producer, I want to set a Markdown CTA in `.worklog/config.yaml` so
    that release reports automatically carry the "play the alpha" prompt.*
- **ContextHub maintainer** — relies on a typed, tested config field so report
  tooling (ship skill, standup, future release reports) can read the CTA
  uniformly without ad-hoc YAML parsing.
  - *As a maintainer, I want the CTA exposed via a documented resolver so
    consumers do not each re-implement config precedence.*
- **Player / community member** — receives the CTA in release output.
  - *As a player, I want release notes to link straight to the playable build
    and a feedback channel.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Typed config field.** `WorklogConfig` exposes an optional `cta?: string`
   field, and `loadConfig()` returns the configured value; unit tests cover the
   value being present, absent (undefined — no behaviour change), and supplied
   via `config.defaults.yaml` / `config.yaml` merge ordering.
2. **Resolver exported.** A single resolver (e.g. `getConfigCta()` /
   `resolveProjectCta()`) is exported from `src/config.ts`, returns the CTA
   string or `null`, and is covered by unit tests including the
   precedence/merge behaviour.
3. **Documented.** `CONFIG.md` documents the `cta` field with a Markdown/YAML
   example, and `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` (or equivalent) shows the field
   shape where appropriate.
4. **Sibling configs populated.** All ten target repositories carry the CTA
   value `[Play the alpha release](<URL>). Provide feedback in [Discord](https://discord.gg/gUKQTFkzQ4)`,
   where `<URL>` = `https://<owner-lowercased>.github.io/<repo>/` derived from
   `git remote get-url origin`. The exact list and derived URLs:

   | Repo | Remote (origin) | CTA URL |
   |---|---|---|
   | AI_Hell | SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell | https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/ |
   | Tableau-Card-Engine | TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine | https://thewizardscode.github.io/Tableau-Card-Engine/ |
   | tce-beleaguered-castle | TheWizardsCode/tce-beleaguered-castle | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-beleaguered-castle/ |
   | tce-blackjack | TheWizardsCode/tce-blackjack | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-blackjack/ |
   | tce-coloretto | TheWizardsCode/tce-coloretto | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-coloretto/ |
   | tce-feudalism | TheWizardsCode/tce-feudalism | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-feudalism/ |
   | tce-golf | TheWizardsCode/tce-golf | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-golf/ |
   | tce-lost-cities | TheWizardsCode/tce-lost-cities | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-lost-cities/ |
   | tce-main-street | TheWizardsCode/tce-main-street | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/ |
   | tce-sushi-go | TheWizardsCode/tce-sushi-go | https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-sushi-go/ |

5. **Missing configs created.** Repositories without a `.worklog/config.yaml`
   (tce-beleaguered-castle, tce-blackjack, tce-feudalism, tce-sushi-go) get a
   minimal config (`projectName`, `prefix`, `cta`); every invented prefix is
   recorded in the work item as a documented assumption.
6. **Testing/validation.** New unit tests exist for the field + resolver; a
   validation step confirms every target repo's `.worklog/config.yaml` parses
   and yields the expected CTA string.
7. **Docs updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **In-repo work (worktree).** The `WorklogConfig` type change, resolver,
  docs, and tests are implemented inside the ContextHub worktree.
- **Out-of-worktree sibling edits (operator-approved exception).** Populating
  the ten sibling repositories modifies files outside the ContextHub worktree.
  Per operator decision (interview Q2 = C) this is an accepted exception to the
  usual "all edits in the worktree" rule; each sibling change is committed in
  its own repository with a message referencing `WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`, and the
  ContextHub commit records the full sibling list.
- **No global agent-infrastructure edits.** Actual report *consumption* (ship
  skill CHANGELOG / Discord notification) is explicitly out of scope and
  deferred to a follow-up work item; global skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills`,
  `.pi/`, repo `skill/`) are not modified.
- **Markdown, YAML-safe.** The `cta` value is a free-form Markdown string; it
  must be quoted correctly in YAML so Markdown link syntax survives round-trip.
- **URL derivation.** Owner/host is lower-cased; repository name preserves
  case (`AI_Hell`, `Tableau-Card-Engine`).
- **Tracking caveat.** Tableau-Card-Engine's `.worklog/` is gitignored and the
  tce-coloretto / tce-golf / tce-lost-cities / tce-main-street `.worklog/`
  trees are currently untracked; the CTA will not be version-controlled there
  unless those repos' ignore rules are also adjusted. This must be surfaced,
  not silently accepted.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` defines `WorklogConfig` (no CTA field);
  `src/types.ts` re-exports it.
- `src/config.ts` implements `loadConfig()` / `loadConfigRelaxed()`, merging
  `config.defaults.yaml` under `config.yaml`, with per-section validators
  (e.g. `validateLlmConfig`, `validateSyncAllowedAuthors`) and resolvers
  (e.g. `resolveLlmConfig`).
- `CONFIG.md` documents the two-tier config override system.
- Sibling config state (verified via `git remote` + `.worklog/config.yaml`):
  AI_Hell (tracked config), Tableau-Card-Engine (config present, `.worklog`
  gitignored), tce-coloretto / tce-golf / tce-lost-cities / tce-main-street
  (config present, `.worklog` untracked), and tce-beleaguered-castle /
  tce-blackjack / tce-feudalism / tce-sushi-go (no config).

## Desired change

1. Add `cta?: string` to `WorklogConfig` with a doc comment describing it as a
   Markdown CTA string surfaced in reports.
2. Add an exported resolver in `src/config.ts` that returns the merged CTA (or
   `null`), mirroring the existing resolver style; optionally validate that a
   present `cta` is a string.
3. Document the field in `CONFIG.md` (and the defaults file where useful) with
   a concrete example.
4. Add unit tests for the type/field round-trip and resolver (present, absent,
   defaults-vs-override merge, non-string rejection if validation is added).
5. Populate (or create) the CTA in every target sibling repository's
   `.worklog/config.yaml`, deriving the URL from the repo's `origin` remote and
   recording each invented `prefix` as an assumption.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — Add `cta?: string` to `WorklogConfig` with a doc comment.
- `src/config.ts` — Add the CTA resolver (and optional `cta` validation), mirroring existing resolver/validator patterns.
- `CONFIG.md` — Document the `cta` field with a YAML/Markdown example.
- `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` — Show/place the field shape where appropriate.
- `tests/unit/config-cta.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for the field, resolver, and merge precedence.
- `<sibling>/.worklog/config.yaml` (×10, out of worktree) — Add/ensure `projectName`, `prefix`, and `cta`.

## Related work

- `Discovery: scan sibling dirs for .worklog/config.yaml (WL-0MP15VRF90070RBT)` — existing sibling-config discovery mechanism, directly reusable if the ten-repo iteration is automated.
- `Fix prefix-to-sibling scan for non-framework repos (WL-0MT6I79640002RR6)` — sibling config discovery fixes.
- `Add .worklog/.config.defaults.yaml (WL-0MKRRZ2DN0WXWH4I)` — config-defaults layering precedent for a `cta` default.
- `Send standup reports to discord using the same webhook as the ship skill (WL-0MURIXAHY0031JIJ)` — a report consumer that could later surface the CTA.
- `Discord summary from structured report (WL-0MLYTLEK00PASLMP)` — precedent for wiring report content into release/notification output.
- `Consume the project CTA in release reports (WL-0MUWEPN6X0044R43)` — the linked follow-up this item blocks; renders the `cta` in release output.

See "## Related work (automated report)" appended by the find-related skill.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLHNPSGP0N397NX** – Do not auto-assign shortcut (completed)
- **WL-0MN9EYA6G009XRZ6** – Review PR #1199 (completed)
- **WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT** – [downtime] Critical items blocked by a filter are never escalated (critical override is dead code) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, card, config, correct, cta, engine, feedback, field, file, form, git, github, hell, https, markdown, over, places, play, project, projects, provide, release, remote, reports, string, tableau, take, tce, url, used, value, where, worklog, yaml
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, card, config, correct, cta, engine, feedback, file, form, git, github, markdown, over, places, play, project, projects, provide, release, remote, string, tableau, take, tce, used, value, where, worklog
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, alpha, config, correct, cta, field, file, form, git, github, hell, hostname, markdown, over, play, project, provide, release, remote, reports, string, take, url, used, value, where, worklog, yaml

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the field name is `cta` (lower-case) and the value is a plain
  Markdown string, per the work-item description.
- **Assumption:** invented prefixes for repos without a config are acceptable;
  they are recorded explicitly for producer review and may be corrected.
- **Risk (scope creep):** report *consumption* (wiring the CTA into the ship
  skill's CHANGELOG / Discord output, standup reports) could expand the item.
  Mitigation: keep this item to the field + resolver + docs + sibling data;
  log consumption as a linked follow-up work item.
- **Risk (trackability):** sibling `.worklog/` trees are gitignored/untracked
  in several repos, so the config change will not persist in version control
  there. Mitigation: surface the tracking gap and, if required, raise it as a
  separate item rather than silently editing.
- **Risk (worktree policy):** out-of-worktree sibling edits may trip the
  implement skill's finish check; the exception is documented and
  operator-approved, and sibling commits are made per-repo.
- **Failure mode:** a malformed/unquoted YAML `cta` breaks config loading for a
  sibling project. Mitigation: validate parsing for every edited config.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: **Q1 — What should this work item actually change?** Options: (A) add typed
  `cta?` field + docs + resolver, report wiring a follow-up; (B) also wire CTA
  into the ship skill release output; (C) only populate sibling configs. —
  Answer (operator, interactive): **A** — "Add typed `cta?` field to
  `WorklogConfig`, document in `CONFIG.md`/defaults, and expose a resolver;
  wire actual report consumption in a follow-up." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: **Q2 — How should sibling config values be applied given the worktree
  rule?** Options: (A) committed helper script run post-merge; (B) one work
  item per repo; (C) populate siblings directly in this item. — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **C** — populate siblings directly, accepting an
  out-of-worktree exception. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: **Q3 — Which projects get a value, and what about those without a
  config?** Options: (A) only repos that already have `.worklog/config.yaml`;
  (B) all 8 tce-* + AI_Hell + Tableau-Card-Engine, creating minimal configs
  where missing; (C) producer-specified subset. — Answer (operator,
  interactive): **B** — all ten repos, creating minimal configs where missing.
  Source: interactive reply.
